record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: Is the symplectic billiard dynamics in the stadium chaotic?

evidence.quote: Question 3: Is the symplectic billiard dynamic in the stadium chaotic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex bounded planar domain with smooth boundary $\gamma = \partial D$. The symplectic billiard map $T$ acts on ordered pairs of boundary points as follows: given $(x,y) \in \gamma \times \gamma$ with $x \neq y$, the image $T(x,y) = (y,z)$ is determined by the condition that the tangent line to $\gamma$ at $y$ is parallel to the chord $xz$ (equivalently, $T$ is the discrete dynamical system on $\gamma \times \gamma$ whose generating function is the symplectic area $\omega(x,y) = \tfrac{1}{2}(x_1 y_2 - x_2 y_1)$, where $\omega$ is the standard area form on $\mathbb{R}^2$).

Now take $D$ to be a stadium: the convex region obtained by joining two congruent semicircles to the two parallel sides of a rectangle (so $\partial D$ consists of two straight segments and two semicircular arcs joined with $C^1$ regularity). To make $\partial D$ smooth, one may also consider a $C^\infty$ rounding of the stadium that preserves its essential geometry (two flat segments connected by strictly convex arcs).

Question: Is the symplectic billiard dynamics $T$ in the stadium chaotic? Specifically, does $T$ possess a subset of positive Lebesgue measure on which it is hyperbolic and has positive metric entropy?
artifact.status_search_result: Symplectic billiards were introduced by Albers and Tabachnikov in 2018. While the standard (Birkhoff) stadium billiard is famously chaotic (Bunimovich), the analogous question for symplectic billiards in a stadium-shaped domain appears in lists of open problems on billiards and geometric optics, and a literature search yields no published proof that symplectic billiards in the stadium are (or are not) chaotic. The status is best described as open.

status_evidence.title: Introducing symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Symplectic billiards introduced as a discrete dynamical system in a strongly convex planar domain with symplectic area as generating function.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the symplectic billiard system used in the problem; chaoticity in the stadium is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Outer symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work extending the symplectic billiards framework; does not resolve chaoticity of the stadium symplectic billiard.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to develop symplectic billiards without settling the stadium chaos question.
